Vehassela immo. heafar shesseviv hashsharashim karuy sela, lefi shehu naase sham kashe kesela. vekaamar sheim haya oto afar immo vehosif alav afar venishrash sham baaretz, roim, im yachol lichyot min heafar shebba immo belo tosefet afar acher, [hare] hu kenatua bimkomo harishon ufatur min haarla, veim lav, hare hu keilan haole meelav vechayyav:
Zizatu hammacharesha. venitpazzer mimmennu heafar venitgallu hashsharashim:
Kofet. chatichat etz ava urechava. vehachi mashma perusho vattosefta:
Serko. tziyyero:
Vechirkemo. tzevao vecharkom:
Veasao fanim. pisselo vemaatzad vehishvahu virhitni, sheyyihyu nirim lo fanim yafim:
Rabbi akiva metamme. demoshav hu:
Vachachamim metaharin. dechachatichat etz bealma chashiv:
Ad sheyyachok. sheyyachkok bo mekom yeshiva:
Hitkinan lishiva tehorim. mimmidras. lefi sheen asuyin lishiva uvatla dato etzel kol adam:
Sergan begemi. al pihen, kederech shemmesargin et hammittot:
Temein. deen hatteven vehammochin yecholin lippol, vachazi lishiva:
Haggozel umaachil. vehinniach lifnehem. o shehinniach lifnehem haggezela kayyemet:

Peturim milleshallem. im achaluha achar mitat avihem veleta beenah, peturim milleshallem, deha inhu lo gazul mide, umittaltele lo mishshabede levaal chov. veim lo achaluha vehi beenah, chayyavim lehachazir:

Veim haya davar sheyyesh bo acharayut. kelomar veim hinniach lahem avihem davar sheyyesh bo acharayut, shehem karkaot, chayyavim leshallem af al pi sheachaluha kevar. hachi mittartza matnitin baggemara. uleinyan pesak halacha, haggozel umaachil et banav, ben sheachlu lifne yeush ben sheachlu leachar yeush, chayyavim leshallem mimmamon shehinniach lahem avihem, ben minnechasim sheyyesh lahem acharayut ben minnechasim sheen lahem acharayut, dehaidna mittalteli mishtabedi levaal chov. veim lo hinniach haggazlan kelum, im achlu habbanim haggezela lifne yeush, chayyavim leshallem mishshellahem. veim leachar yeush achlu, en chayyavim leshallem mishshellahem ella im ken hinniach lahem avihem:
En portin. en machlifim selaim bifrutot:
Mittevat hammochsin. littol perutot mittevatan shennotnim bah meot hammeches:

Velo mikkis shel gabbaim. gabbay hammelech sheggove kesef gulgolet vearnona. lefi shehen shel gazel. vedavka bemoches nachri o moches yisrael sheen lo kitzba, shellokeach kemo shehu rotze. aval moches yisrael sheheemido afillu melech nachri velokeach davar katzuv bechak hammalchut, eno bechezkat gazlan, ufortin mittevato. velo od ella sheasur lehaveriach min hammeches shello, dedina demalchuta dina:
Mittoch beto. shel moches shehu bechezkat gazlan:

O min hashshuk. im yesh lo maot beveto o bashshuk sheenam betevat hammeches. veim chayyav adam perutot lammoches bachatzi dinar veen lo perutot. noten lo dinar kesef umekabbel mimmennu perutot beshave chetzyo, veaf al pi shennoten lo mittevat hammeches, mippene shehu kematztzil miyyado:
Notim yichur shel arla. shehaetz muttar bahanaa. aval lo haegoz shehu peri veasur bahanaa. umode rabbi yose sheim nata vehivrich vehirkiv shehu muttar, deze veze gorem muttar:

Bechafniyyot. yichur sheyyesh bo kafniyyot, temarim beodan semadar nikraim kafniyyot. rabbi yose letaameh deamar hassemadar asur mippene shehu peri. vahalacha kemoto demuttar litta yichur shel arla, veen halacha kemoto sheoser bechafniyyot:
Hachittim enan mitztarfot im hakkol. im hayu shete issot, achat shel chittim veachat shel min acher mechameshet hamminim, veen beachat mehen shiur challa, venoshchot zo vazo:
Hasseorim mitztarfot im hakkol. af im hakkussemin, veaf al gav demin chittim hen, lav davka min chittim ella min seorim veaf min chittim, vehachi parishna la beresh perek kamma:
Shear hamminim mitztarfin ze im ze. kegon kussemin veshibbolet shual veshifon. vahalacha kerabbi yochanan ben nuri:
Yittol min haemtza. mimmakom shennoshchin ze et ze, nimtza mafrish mishshetehen:
Vachachamim osrim. sheharoe savur shemmuttar litrom uleasser min hechadash al hayyashan umin hayyashan al hechadash. vahalacha kachachamim:
Min hakkav. sheen bo shiur challa:
Rabbi akiva omer challa. vehu shehishlim al haissa achar ken keshiur challa, dechevan shennishlam hashshiur haveya challa lemafrea:
Enah challa. kevan shebbeshaa shehifrishah hayta haissa petura. vahalacha kachachamim:
Shennittal chippuyo haemtzai. shennittal luach haemtzai venishar luach mikkan veluach mikkan:
Tame. dachazi lishiva:
Im haya rachav tefach. chazi lishiva. veim lo, lo:
Haggozel. meshallem kishat haggezela. deme etzim vetzemer. veen chayyav lehachezir lo kelim, dekane beshinnuy:
Deme rachel haomedet liggazez. vehaodef sheshshave yoter havvalad vehaggizza, shello hu, diknannehu beshinnuy:

Ze hakkelal. laatoye ganav tale venaasa ayil, egel venaasa shor, utevacho o mecharo, shehu patur mittashlume arbaa vachamishsha, shekkevan shennaasa shinnuy beyado, kenao, veshello hu toveach veshello hu mocher:
En lokchin min haroim. deikka lememar shemma ganvu mitztzono shel baal habbayit hammasur lahem:
Tzemer bihuda ufishtan baggalil. melechet hannashim hi, vehen atzman osot umochrot. uledaat baalehen hu:
Vaagalim haroim bashsharon. shem makom shemmegaddelin bo agalim. veshellahen hen:
Kekattedra. shehi ketzara umukkefet mishshalosh ruchot:
Temea midras. dimyuchedet lishiva:
Kemitta. shehi arukka umeyuchedet lehanniach bah perakmatya, vehashshochev bah omrim lo amod venaase melachtenu:
Veshel avanim. haasuya leholich bah avanim:
Tehora mikkelum. lefi shepperutza mittachtitah nekavim gedolim kemotzi rimmon:

Shete nashim. afillu hen mimmin echad peturim. veen neshicha vetzeruf sal metzarfan, kevan shemmakpidot. vaafillu lashu shene kabbin keechad, kevan desofan lechalek peturot. usetam matnitin kevet hillel deamre kabbayim lachalla, veenah halacha, dekayma lan dachamishsha revaim hu shiur challa:
Uvizman shehen shel ishsha achat. setam ishsha achat enah makpedet im haissot nogot zo vazo:
Min bemino chayyav. binshicha o vetzeruf sal:
Hannotea lisyag. sheyyihye hailan gader lakkerem:
Ulekorot. legaddel etzim laasot mehen korot levinyan, veen ikkar netiato leechol happerot:
Patur min haarla. dichtiv (Vayikra 19) unetatem kol etz maachol, et shehu lemaachol chayyav, lisyag ulekorot uleetzim patur:
Happenimi lemaachol. nitkavven sheyyichur penimi yihye lemaachol veyichur hachitzon lisyag, af al pi shehakkol ilan echad, hachitzon patur. veen halacha kerabbi yose:
Hare ellu shello. demistama nityaashu habbealim miyyad, ukenanhu haich beyeush veshinnuy reshut:

Im nityaashu habbealim. deshaminhu deiyyaesh, deamre vay lechesron kis. aval setama lo. veresha denatlu listim et kesuto demashma demistama mityaashu, mayre belistim yisrael, dechevan dedayyane yisrael amre have edim have reaya, mikki natlu lo listim miyyaesh. vesefa belistim nachrim, sheddayyane nachrim danin begaava uvizroa uveumdan daat belo edim velo reaya, vehannigzal mehem lo miyyaesh. umishshum hachi i shaminhu deiyyaush in, aval setama lo:
Nachil shel devorim. kibbutz shennikbatzim im hammelech shellahem:
Lo yakotz et socho. nityashshevu devorim [shello] al sochat chavero, veyare littelan echad echad, shello yivrechu, lo yakotz et hassocha kullah, vaafillu al menat litten et haddamim:
Rabbi yishmael kulei. veen halacha kerabbi yishmael:
Chamatot. nodot shel or:
Turemlin. kisin gedolim shel or, sheharoe manniach chafatzav letochan:

Hamekabbelim kashshiur. hameforash lemala beresh perek karim, hachemet shel shivat kabbim, vehatturemel shel chameshet kabbin. vechol shekken im machazikim yoter, deaz meshammeshim yeshiva im melachtan. aval pachot mikkan lo:
Veshel or haddag tehorim mikkelum. dechol habba mibberiyyot shebbayyam, tahor:
Venishba lo al hachomesh. shevua sheniyya, shennetano lo, vehoda shello netano:
Hare ze meshallem chomesh al chomesh. chumsho shel chomesh, dechomesh rishon naase keren:

Ad sheyyitmaet vechulei. sheim chazar venatan lo chomesh rishon venishba al hashsheni vehoda, meshallem chumsho vechumsho shel chomesh sheni, vechen leolam. shenneemar (sham) vachamishitav yosef alav, hattora ribbeta chamishiyyot harebe lekeren echad:
Tesumet yad. halevaa:
Ashak et amito. sechar sachir:
Meshallem keren. deen chomesh veasham ella im ken hoda. dichtiv begezel hagger befarashat naso, vehitvadda:

Haomer lachavero gezalticha vechulei. uchegon shechavero toano bari gezaltani, vehu omer emet, gezalticha, aval eni yodea im hechezarti lecha, chayyav leshallem. aval im chavero toen shemma gezaltani o hilveticha, vehu omer emet gezalticha o hilvetani veeni yodea im hechezarti lecha, patur middine adam. veim ba latzet yede shamayim, yeshallem lo:

Eni yodea im gezalticha vechulei‏ patur milleshallem. umihu yishshava sheeno yodea shechayyav lo, delo adif shemma mibbari, deha i nammi hava taen leh en lecha beyadi kelum, hava mashbeinan leh shevuat hesset:
Leshatiach. lishtoach baaretz leshev alav:
Letachrich hakkelim. lichroch bo et hakkelim, kegon sakkinim umisparayim umechatim kede leshamran:
Veshel retzuot veshel sandalim. or haomed lachtoch mimmennu retzuot vesandalim, tahor mikkelum, dimchussar melacha hu. aval retzuot hametukkanot kevar, temeot, kidmuchach bemassechet negaim perek 11:
Hattokea lachavero. shemmechabber etzbeotav befas yado umakke oto baegrof:
Noten lo sela. deme bashto. veen halacha kerabbi yose sheomer mane:
Setaro. shehikkahu befas yado al lechyo, veikka boshet tefe:
Tzaram. mashach. lashon acher, pagam:
Hakkol lefi kevodo. kol ellu haddamim shehuzkeru bammishna enam ella limchubbad beyoter. aval leadam bazuy pochatin lo:
Amar rabbi akiva vechulei. rabbi akiva paleg attanna kamma, vesavar deven mechubbad ben bazuy, kullan shavin ledine kenasot hallalu. veen halacha kerabbi akiva:
Venatan lo zeman. vehane mille levoshet, delo chassereh mamona, yahavinan zeman. aval linzakin, dechassereh mamona, lo yahavinan zeman:
Shemarah. himtin lah ad sheraa otah omedet al petach chatzerah:
Uvo keissar shemen. shemen kanuy beissar:
Lazo ani noten arba meot zuz. sheal keissar shemen zilzela beatzmah legallot roshah umara hi sheenah makpedet al habboshet:
Shene kabbin. shel echad mechameshet hamminim shechayyavin bachalla:
Vekav orez o teruma. sheen chayyavin bachalla, baemtza:
En mitztarfin. lehitchayyev bachalla:
Shelosha terisin hen. shelosha dinim chalukin ze mizze yesh bitrisin, dehaynu maginnim:
Teris hakkafuf. hammetzuyin etzlenu, shemmakkifim et haadam mishshalosh ruchot:
Tame midras. deasuy lishchiva, sheshshochvim alav bammilchama. vechol shekken shettame teme met, dekayma lan kol hattame midras tame teme met:

Shemmesachakim bo bakkumpon. bassade shel emek hammelech, baim shenayim kol echad charbo veyado uteris katan agol sheeno chafuf beyado hassemalit, ulemedin lehagen kol echad bemaginno shello yakkehu chavero. vekorin lo 754 belaaz:
Tame teme met. vehu haddin shettame tumat sheretz unevela ushear tumot kullan, chutz mimmidras, sheeno naase av hattuma im shachav alav hazzav o yashav, ella rishon kemaggao shel zav:
Veditzat haarviyyin. teris katan beyoter shehaarviyyim osim leditza ulesimcha velischok, veeno cheli shel tashmish:
Netaluha mesikin. annasim gezaluha min haggazlan. targum tzelatzal, sakkaa. shehaarbe gazlan hu, sheochel bisdot acherim:
Im makkat medina hi. sheansu karka shel acherim im zo:
Tarbusim. kelim shel or keen argazim:
Shel sapparim. makkizim dam:
Tame midras. gadol hu vachazi lishiva o lemizga aleh:
Sheochlim alav. keli tashmish hu:
Veshel zetim. shessochatin bo hazzetim, la chashiv keli shel meshammeshe adam:
Rabbi akiva foter. veazda letaameh dehadra vehaveya challa lemafrea:

Nimtza chumro kullo. chumro shel rabbi akiva deamar leel benotel challa mikkav dehavya challa vekiddeshah, gorem lo lehakel veliftor bishne kabbim shennittela challato shel ze bifne atzmo veshel ze bifne atzmo:
Chalak maggao mimmassao. denose metamme vegadim veen nogea metamme vegadim:
Tafit shel chamor. etzim shennotnim al gav hachamor lechabber velikshor alehem hammassa. veenan reuyin lo lirchiva velo lishiva:
Shinna et hannekavim. divshinnuy nikvehen noten makom leadam leshev sham:

O sheppertzan. shehesiram mimmekomam unetanan ze letzad ze. veyesh mefarshim, tafit shel chamor tehora lefi sheen berachbah tefach, vechol sheen berachbah tefach lo chazi lishiva, uchesheshshinna et hannekavim dehaynu shehirchiv mekom hammoshav o sheppertzan venaasa mekom hammoshav rachav tefach, temea:
Shenneemar veim en laish goel. veen lecha adam beyisrael sheen lo goalim lemala ad yaakov avinu ella ze hagger shemmet veen lo yorshin:
Umet. haggazlan:
Hakkesef yinnaten levanav. shel gazlan. shekkevar zacha bahen mimmitat hagger, ella dahashava bae lemeevad ki hechi deteheve leh kappara ashshevuateh, vehasheta tu lekka kappara kevan demit leh:
Vehaasham yire. kedin asham shemmetu bealav, dekayma lan kol shebbechattat meta beasham roe:
Ad sheyyistaev. ad sheyyippol bo mum:
Veyippelu damav lindava. leketz hammizbeach liknot mehem olot:
Ume gefanim. hammayim hayyotzim min haggefanim keshechotchim otam o et hazzemorot bime nisan:
Hassemadar. hu happerach shemmimmennu yatza habboser. aval habboser atzmo hakkol modim shehu peri:
Muttarim baarla. dichtiv (Vayikra 19) vaaraltem arlato et piryo, vehanne lav peri ninhu:
Uvarvai. neechalin beshana reviit chutz lirushalayim belo fidyon, deyihye kol piryo kodesh hillulim ketiv (sham), vehanne lo have peri:
Uvannazir. muttar hannazir leachlam, devannazir ketiv (Bamidbar 6) lo yochal, vehanne lav bene achila ninhu:
Vaasurim baashera. dichtiv (Devarim 13) velo yidbak beyadcha meuma min hacherem, vaashera hu ilan hanneevad:

Hammaamid bisraf haarla. hammaamid gevina bassaraf hannotef meatze arla: saraf. 50 belaaz. vesavar rabbi eliezer desaraf have peri, ben beilan haose ferot, ben beilan sheeno ose ferot. veen halacha kerabbi yose velo cherabbi eliezer:
Bisraf happaggim. saraf hannotef min happerot shello vashlu kol tzarkan. vahalacha kerabbi yehoshua:

Teva sheppitchah mitztziddah. meshammeshet yeshiva im melachtah, sheyyecholim lehishtammesh bah keshehu yoshev, bizman sheppitchah mitztziddah. ma sheen ken kesheppitchah millemalan. vehabbaa vemidda ditninan bematnitin shehi tehora mikkelum, aenah meyuchedet lemidras kae, dehattemea midras afillu vaa vemidda leolam hi temea:
Tashlume chefel. veim hoda meatzmo eno meshallem kefel, dichtiv (Shemot 22) asher yarshiun elohim, perat lemarshia et atzmo:
Ankoklot. leshon notrikon, anavim delaku telat. kelomar shellaku kodem sheheviu shelish bishshulan:
Hachartzannim. garinim shebbetoch haanavim:
Vehazzaggim. hakkelippot shebbachutz:
Vehattemed. shennatan mayim al gabbe shemarim o al gabbe hachartzannim vehazzaggin, veyesh bahem taam yayin:
Vehannetz shellahen. perach sheal gabbe happitma:
Vehaggarinin. garin shel kol peri, kegon haggarinim hannimtzaim betoch hattemarim vehazzetim vehaafarsekim, vechayyotze vahen:
Asurim baarla. dichtiv (Vayikra 19) et piryo, et hattafel lefiryo:
Umuttarim barvai. shenneta revai eno asur bahanaa, ella neechol labbealim birushalayim kemaaser sheni. veen mitkaddesh bikdushshat maaser sheni ella davar harauy laachila:
Novlot. perot hannoshrim min hailan kodem gemar bishshulan:
Kullan asurot. ben baarla ben barvai ben baashera ben bannazir:
Chutz mippachot mishshave feruta vechulei. velo chayshinan shemma yityakker veyashuv al shave peruta, vaafillu haggazel been eno tzarich leholicho acharav:
Peraklinin. tzurat yad shel or shennosim tzayyade ofot keshettofsim bidehen haof shekkorin 516 veshfrvyr, uvo yotzim latzud chayya o of:
Tame midras. lefi shennishan alav:
Veshel chagavim. haholchim latzud chagavim venotnim otam bo:
Veshel kotzim. lilkot kotzim. veit degarse shel kayyatzim, hameyabbeshim perot hakkayitz, kegon haosim gerogarot vetzimmukim bassade:
Shalosh pinkasiyyot hen. haasuyin lichtov bahen. kemo chenvani al pinkaso:
Efiforin. luach shemmannichim alav avak shel afar vechotvim bo cheshbonot. vegadol hu vachazi lishiva:
Sheyyesh lah bet kibbul shaava. luach shettachin panav bedonag veroshmin al haddonag becheret:
Vachalaka. sheen bah shaava, vechotvim aleha bidyo, veen lah bet kibbul:

Hammitta vehakkar vehakkeset shel met. af al gav demet eno metamme midras vehanach lammet asuyin velo leshev alehen, afillu hachi temeim midras, mippene shehannashim yoshvot alehen [umevakkot et metehen]:
Umashber shel chayya. moshav haishsha hayyoledet. al haavnayim (Shemot 1) metargeminan al matbera:
Shehu chorem alav. garsinan. kelomar mekappel umetakken sham et habbegadim:

Amar rabbi yose en bahen mishshum moshav. umatnitin defirkin dilel ditnan kisse shel kalla shennittelu chippuyav demashma ha lo nittelu chippuyav tame, peliga adderabbi yose. veen halacha kerabbi yose:

Hammakkir kelav usefarav vechulei. matnitin beadam sheeno asuy limkor kelav, dechevan deyatza lo shem geneva bair, veikka sahade sheellu hakkelim vehassefarim shello hayu, lo chayshinan dilma ihu zabbeninhu:
Yishshava lokeach kamma natan veyittol. veyachzir lo kelav. velifne yeush kamayre:

Hatteruma. olin beechad umea. im nafla sea achat meellu bemea sein shel chullin betela umuttarim lezarim. befachot mimmea, hakkol asur lezarim. umafkinan la middichtiv gabbe terumat maaser (Bamidbar 18) et mikdesho mimmennu, ma shehuram mimmennu im chazar letocho mekaddesho, dehaynu tishim vetisha, demimmea hifrish asara lemaaser, umeasara achat litrumat maaser:

Umitztarfin ze im ze. im nafla sea achat mikkullan lefachot mimmea chullin mekaddashtan. uveha modu kulle alma demitztarfin, deshem echad ninhu vechulehu mikkaryan teruma devachalla ketiv (sham 15) challa tarimu teruma, uvikkurim nammi ikru teruma, deamar mar uterumat yadecha ellu bikkurim dichtiv behu (Devarim 26) velakach hakkohen hattene miyyadecha:

Vetzarich leharim. hassea shennafla velatet otah lakkohen, vehashshear muttar lezarim. veaf al gav divarla vechile hakkerem dachamire tefe en tzarich leharim vehaissur atzmo batel, shane teruma deyesh lah bealim vetzarich leharim mippene gezel hashshevet, aval bechol shear issurim delo shayyach behu din gazel, keshehen mitbattelin en tzarich leharim:

Olin beechad umatayim. degabbe teruma ketiv melea, (Shemot 22) meleatcha vedimacha lo teacher, uvechile hakkerem ketiv melea, (Devarim 22) pen tikdash hammelea, ma melea haamur lehallan ola, kidyalfinan meet mikdesho mimmennu, af kan ola. ulefi shekkafal issuro, shehu asur bahanaa, kaflu aliyyato vetzarich matayim. vearla yalfinan la mikkilayim lefi shehi asura bahanaa kemotan:
Umitztarfin ze im ze. arla vechile hakkerem meoravin yachad shennaflu letoch hetter, mitztarfin leesor beyavesh ad matayim, uvelach bikdera benoten taam:
Enan mitztarfin. afillu leesor hakkedera benoten taam, kevan dishne shemot ninhu. ella im yesh bakkedera levattel taam haarla bifne atzman, vetaam kile hakkerem bifne atzman, hakkol muttar:
Mitztarfin benoten taam. shetztzarich bakkedera belach kede levattel taam shetehen yachad:
Aval lo leesor. beyavesh, sheen tzarich sheyyihye bahetter matayim keneged shetehen. vahalacha ketanna kamma:

Al menat latzet bammidbar. lo sheyyomar lo beferush al menat shettetze bammidbar vetifreeni, deha milleta difshita hi. ella kegon sheamar lo chavero leheve hay pikkadon gabbach, daana lammidbar nafekna. vaamar leh idach vaana nammi lammidbar baena lemefak, vehasheta i bae leahdorinhu bammidbar mahadar lehu:
Baavadim omer lo hare shellecha lefanecha. dichkarka damu uvirshuta demarayhu kayyeme. vahalacha kerabbi meir:
Matbea venisdak. shinnuy hannikkar hu:
Perot vehirkivu. keshehirkivu miktzatan [omer lo hare shellecha lefanecha ]. aval hirkivu kullam, meshallem kishat haggezela:
Matbea venifsal. sheeno over beotah medina, aval over hu bimdina acheret:
Veneevda vah avera. shennirbea o neevda [laavoda zara] shehi pesula lekarban:
Shennifsela lammizbeach. bemum sheeno nikkar kegon bedokin shebbaayin:
En lo ella secharo. sechar keli usechar peulla:

Shataf nahar chamoro. tzericha lemitne tere bave dematnitin. dei tana resha hava amena hatam hu dechi paresh yahev leh deme kullah mishshum devayyadayim ka pased, sheshshafach et yeno bayyadayim bishvilo, aval sefa demimmela, ema en lo ella secharo. vei ashmoinan sefa, hacha hu devistama en lo ella secharo mishshum demimmela, aval hatam devayyadayim, ema afillu bistama yahev leh deme kullah. tzericha:
Shidda. asuya chemin aron. uveshidda sheenah machzeket arbaim sea mayre, shehi mekabbelet tuma:
Shennittal haelyon. hakkissuy shealeha:
Hattachton. shuleha:
Nittal haelyon vehattachton. vehaddappin shebbatztzedadin nisharu:
Vachachamim metaharin. vahalacha kachachamim:
Hassattat. mesattet avanim. vehu metakken lo makom lashevet bekatze haechad mehaeven keshemmesattet bakkatze hashsheni:
Zarez haashkeloni. chagora rechava shebbah chovshim et habbehema. targum vayyachavosh et chamoro, vezarez (Bereshit 22) uveashkelon osim otan shel etz, ukeruyin zarez ashkeloni al shem mekoman:

Medocha hammadit. machteshet haasuya vemaday. lokchim chatichat etz gedola ava vaarukka, vechokkim kemin machteshet beemtzaah, verochvim aleha mikkan umikkan vechotshim. ulefichach yesh alav torat merkav:
Avit shel gamal. targum bechar haggamal, baavita degamla (sham lo):

Tappetan shel sus. ukkaf sheal hassus bilshon mishna tappetan shemo, veshel gamal avit shemo, veshel naka ukkaf shemo, kol echad shemo alav. vechullan merkav hen, ella sheyyesh mehen sheppeamim asuyin leshev alehen:
Tappetan shel sus tame moshav. deen tame merkav ella hameyuchad lirchiva befissuk raglayim, veeno asuy lishiva chelal:
Bakkunpon. sade shessochakim sham hammelachim, uregilim lashevet al hattappetan shel sus lirot bischok hammelech, hilkach tame moshav. kunepon, sade, bilshon 107 236. veen halacha kerabbi yose:

Aval ukkaf shel naka tame. rambam peresh, tame moshav. vetanna kamma kaamar la, defaleg attappetan shel sus umode veukkaf shel naka shehu tame moshav. verabbotay pershu, aval ukkaf shel naka tame merkav. verabbi yose kaamar la, demode letanna kamma beukkaf shel naka sheeno meyuchad ella lirchiva:
Hannotel seor meissat chittin. shello hurema challatah:
Veim lav petura. deen hattevel osrah, kevan delekka taam:

Im ken lamma amru hattevel oser bechol shehu. deamran leel kesheen lo parnasa shemmevi al hakkol. hanne mile bemino, aval shello vemino ki hay dechittin beorez, benoten taam, detaama detevel bechol shehu, mishshum dichhettero dechitta achat poteret et hakkeri, kach issuro, vehay taama lo shayyach ella min bemino:
Mibbetar. shem makom bechutz laaretz:

Velo kibbelu mimmennu. dilachlan i efshar shehare nitmeu veeretz haammim. ulesarfan i efshar lefi sheen tuma zo yedua, shemma yomru rainu teruma tehora nisrefet, lehachaziran limkoman i efshar shello yomru teruma yotza meeretz yisrael lechutz laaretz, ella mannichan ad erev pesach vesorfan:
Vechag hakkatzir bikkure maasecha. dishte hallechem ikru bikkurim, umattirin et hechadash bammikdash:

Kisse shello hayu chippuyav yotzim. sheen hannesarim boltim chutz min hakkisse. shehakkisse asuy mearbaa etzim unesarim kevuin mishshelosh ruchot hakkisse omdin gevohim tachat haetzim mehuddakim ze etzel ze, umimmaal laetzim luchot asuyin leshev alehen. veim nishberu halluchot haasuyot lemoshav, yachol lehattot hakkisse lechol tzad sheyyirtze veleshev al otan hannesarim hakkevuim beshalosh ruchot shel kisse, aval keshehen boltim lachutz eno yachol lehattoto al tziddo. vechippuyav dehacha lav kechippuyav deresha shehen kemo shinnayim boltim, ella lannesarim shemmechappin haetzim kare chippuyav:
Shalosh aratzot. chalukot bedin challa:
Meeretz yisrael vead keziv. kelomar kol eretz yisrael ad keziv, shehi retzua hayyotza meakko letzad tzafon, uchevashuha ole vavel vekadsha kedushsha sheniyya:
Mafrishim challa echat. venittenet lakkohen veochlah betohora:

Mikkeziv vead hannahar. letzad mizrach umikkeziv vead amana letzad maarav. veenah eretz yisrael mammash, lefi shekkevashuha ole mitzrayim velo chevashuha ole vavel, ukedushsha rishona lo kadsha leatid lavo:

Mafrishin shete challot. harishona nisrefet lefi shehi temea betumat eretz haammim, kevan shello chevashuha ole vavel, vehashsheniyya neechelet lefi sheen tumat hachalla harishona mefursemet, shehare enah eretz haammim gemura. veim lo hayu mafrishin challa sheniyya hanneechelet yomru teruma tehora nisrefet, aval keshemmafrishin challa sheniyya veneechelet haroe noten al libbo lehavin taam haddavar, o shoel lachachamim veomrim lo:
Shel ur yesh lah shiur. mippene shezzot haaretz hayta kedosha kevar, niret challatah keshel tora, hilkach yafrish kashshiur shemmafrishim meissa temea, echad meesrim vearbaa o mearbaim ushemona:
Veshel kohen en lah shiur. lefi shehi middivre sofrim:

Min hannahar umin amana velifnim. kelomar mittechillat hannahar velifnim mimmenna, vechen mittechillat amana velifnim mimmennu, chutza laaretz mammash, umafrishin shete challot ushetehen middivre sofrim:
Achat laur. shehi temea betumat eretz haammim mammash:
Veachat lakkohen. kede shello tishtakkach torat challa shennittenet lakkohen:
Shel ur en lah shiur. hoil ushetehen middivre sofrim, mutav leharebot beotah shennotnin lakkohen shenneechelet velo vannisrefet:

Utevul yom ochlah. lechallat haur shel chutz yisrael. utevul yom dekaamar hacha hu kohen shettaval lekeryo, sheen challat haur shel chutz yisrael asura ella lemi shettuma yotza alav miggufo, aval tame vishar tumot muttar bah. hilkach bechutz laaretz hecha deikka kohen katan shello raa keri miyyamav o kohen gadol bashshanim shettaval lekeryo, mafrish challa achat bilvad venotnah lakkohen. vei lekka kohen katan o kohen gadol shettaval lekeryo veikka kohen baal keri, mafrish shete challot, achat laur veen lah shiur, veachat lakkohen veyesh lah shiur, echad mearbaim ushemona, kedin kol issa shennitmea veones, detumat eretz haammim tumat ones hi, veochlah hakkohen bekeryo, kede shello tishtakkach torat challa miyyisrael:
Eno tzarich tevila. uvaal keri muttar bechallat chutz yisrael. veen halacha kerabbi yose:
Vaasura lazzavim velazzavot. rabbanan kaamre la, deillu lerabbi yose sharya lazzavim velazzavot ki hechi desharya levaal keri:
Veneechelet im hazzar al hashshulchan. delo gazrinan haalaa atu achila:

Venittenet lechol kohen. ben lechohen chaver ben lechohen am haaretz, kach peresh rambam. veen shitat haggemara mochachat ken, ella ben lechohen sheochel chullav betohora, ben lechohen sheeno ochel chullav betohora, aval leam haaretz en notnin shum mattana mimmattenot kehunna dichtiv (divrei hayamim 2 lo) latet menat hakkohanim vehaleviyyim lemaan yechezku betorat Adonai, en notnin mana ella lechohanim hammachazikim betorat Adonai‏. vechen ha ditnan lekamman ellu nittanin lechol kohen, lav lechohen am haaretz, ella lechol kohen af al pi sheeno ochel chullav betohora:
Shel zaggagim. shemmannichim aleha kele zechuchit:
Saragin. ose hammerkavot. baaravi korin lemerkav 273. veyesh mefarshim, shemmesargim et hassevachot. utehora mikkelum lefi sheenah mimmeshammeshe adam:
Hacharamim. lakkohanim kedichtiv (Bamidbar 18) kol cherem beyisrael lecha yihye:
Vehabbechorot. i tam hu hare ze kadshe mikdash, vei vaal mum hu ketiv (Devarim 12) hattame vehattahor yochlennu:
Ufidyon peter chamor. podehu vese veen bo kedushsha:
Reshit haggez. dichtiv (sham 18) vereshit gez tzoncha titten lo:
Veshemen serefa. shemen teruma shennitma:

Vekadshe mikdash. delo asru latet lechohen sheeno nizhar mittuma ella davar sheyyesh bo issur tuma baggevulin, kegon teruma uterumat maaser vechalla, aval kadshe mikdash uvikkurim shemmeviin otam laazara, lo chashshu, detihure metaher nafsheh:
Rabbi yehuda oser babbikkurim. dechayesh dilma lo mizdaher behu, hoil veen osin bahen avoda. veen halacha kerabbi yehuda:
Rabbi akiva mattir. rabbi akiva letaameh, deamar beferek sheni demaaser sheni decharshinin kol maasehen betuma, delo chashive ochel:
Vachachamim osrim. dachashive lehu ochel hoil vehen neechalin bishnot reavon. vahalacha kachachamim:
Hakkaddur. 126 belaaz:
Vehaimmum. defus shel minal. vechol ellu chitzonehem or umelein mibbifnim sear o mochin:
Vehakkamea vehattefillin. yesh betoch habbattim shel or parashiyyot ketuvot biklaf:
Uvema shebbetochan tahor. im nitma achat meellu vemet veachar kach nikra, venaga echad bema shebbetochan, tahor, lefi sheen ma shebbetochan chibbur lahen veen ma shebbetochan tame chemotan:
Hakkauf. kemo ukkaf:
Hannogea bema shebbetocho tame. im nitma haukkaf bemet, keshem shehannogea bo tame, kach hannogea bema shebbetocho tame:
Mippene shehattefer mechabbero. veosehu echad, ze shebbifnim im hachitzon:

Veim en lo. ma yochal, love veochel. uvaale chov baim venifraim min hayerushsha et chelko. velo chashiva hanaa ma shepporea chovo beotam maot, deha tenan bindarim [daf log] hammudar hanaa mechavero porea lo chovo:

rashi: Tiferet bachurim kocham. kemo shettiferet bachurim kocham, ken hadrat zekenim seva:
targum: Shivhora deulemaya tukefehon ushevacha desave siveta:

rashi: Chabburot petza tamruk bera. dareshu rabbotenu (yalkut shemauni mishlei tatakanat): hamemarek atzmo lidvar avera, sof ba lide petzaim vechabburot:
Umakkot chadre vaten. ze hahidrokan (Bava Metzia 107:):
targum: Shuchane ufudeata pegau vevisha umachyata begavah dichresa:

Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 11:161-172: And concerning this it is said in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 145a): we have learned, any person who has piety in him is called "an angel of the LORD of Hosts" - this is what is written (Malachi 2:7), "for the priest's lips should keep knowledge, and Torah they should seek from his mouth, for he is an angel of the LORD of Hosts." And he says, just as Michael is a priest above, from the side of Chesed, so the priest, from the side of Chesed, is an angel of the LORD below; and a person who has piety in him enters beyond the letter of the law with every person - it follows that he does not conduct himself according to the nature of this world, which was created according to the letter of the law, but according to the World to Come, which was created with the yud (Menachot 29b), which is the right, Chochmah, the root of Chesed (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 227b) - and therefore piety is greater than all of them.

And on the verse "preserve my soul, for I am pious" (Psalms 86:2), this matter is brought (in the Yalkut, ibid., remez 834), and in another version: whoever hears his own disgrace, and it is within his power to protest, but is silent, is called "chassid" - and this version appears more correct.

And further, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 4a): Rabbi Levi and Rabbi Yitzchak - one said, David said this before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, am I not pious, that all the kings of east and west sleep until the third hour of the day, while I rise at midnight to give thanks to You? And the other said, David said this before the Holy One, blessed be He: Master of the universe, am I not pious, that all the kings of east and west sit in groups in their honor before them, while my hands are soiled with the blood of a fetus and the afterbirth, in order to purify a woman for her husband; and not only that, but everything I do, I take counsel with Mefivoshet my teacher, and say to him, Mefivoshet my teacher, have I judged rightly, have I found guilty rightly, have I acquitted rightly, have I declared impure rightly, have I declared pure rightly - and I was not ashamed. Rabbi Yehoshua the son of Rav Idi said, what verse [supports this]? (Psalms 119:46), "and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings, and will not be ashamed" - to this point.

We learn from this discourse that one who rises at midnight is called "chassid." And likewise, one who makes himself small before one greater than himself, and is not ashamed to ask him a matter of Torah law, is called "chassid." And the verse Rabbi Yehoshua brought, "and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings," we are compelled to say refers, by "kings," to the Sages, as they say (Gittin 62a), "who are 'kings'? These are the Rabbis." And in general we learn from this discourse that anyone who does a thing not obligatory upon him by the law of the Torah is called "chassid" for these matters mentioned in the discourse - to purify a woman for her husband, and the rest.

Further, among the branches of Chesed is that he rebuke his fellow - and this is an act of kindness, for he does kindness with that soul; and one who is rebuked should accept his fellow's rebuke for the sake of Heaven, and consider that rebuke a kindness done to him, since through it he is saved from the judgment of Gehinnom, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 141:5), "let the righteous strike me, it shall be a kindness; and let him rebuke me." And concerning the matter of rebuke, we elaborated in the Gate of Humility, chapter 5.

Further, among the branches of Chesed is trust in the LORD, as it is said (ibid. 32:10), "but he who trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him." And they said in Midrash Vayikra Rabbah: Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Tanchum - even a wicked person, if he trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him - to this point. And the intent is that they expounded the juxtaposition of the verse, "many are the sorrows of the wicked; but he who trusts."

And further our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Bava Kamma 30a): whoever wishes to be pious should fulfill the matters of Berachot [blessings], and the matters of Nezikin [damages], and the matters of Avot [ethics] - to this point. And the reason for the matters of Berachot is that because he is of a good eye, he shall be blessed, as explained above. And likewise the matters of Nezikin, because one who damages his fellow becomes a portion of the judgment of Gevurah to strike his fellow, and he distances himself from Chesed, which benefits all - therefore he must learn Nezikin so as not to come to damage his fellow. And the matters of Avot are self-evident.

Further, in order to merit Chesed, one must be a God-fearing person, as it is said (Psalms 103:17), "but the kindness of the LORD is from everlasting to everlasting upon those who fear Him" - for the ascent of the levels from below upward is: first one enters through fear, and afterward through Chesed - for the Shechinah is called "fear" (Ra'aya Meheimna, Parashat Pinchas, page 229b), and one must hold fast to the particulars of fear that are in her, and afterward ascend to the world of the male, which is Chesed - for the Righteous One [Yesod] is called "Chesed," as explained in the Idra (Parashat Naso, page 142a). And likewise, Chesed [and] Gevurah - Gevurah is called "fear," and one must be careful of the negative commandments, and afterward he shall merit Chesed, which is the fulfillment of the positive commandments; and the particulars of fear are the attributes mentioned - alacrity, cleanliness, purity - and further particulars will be explained in the Gate of Holiness. And all the attributes we have explained in this Gate are the levels that lead to being a chassid.

And in the Zohar (Parashat Naso, page 145b), they explained on this verse that whoever merits fear merits humility and piety - Rabbi Elazar said, whoever has fear, humility, and piety in him has the sum of all in him. And he said there that "yerei'av" [those who fear Him] refers to the sum of male and female, which is "Adam" - and whoever joins male and female is called "Adam," and then he fears sin, and not only that, but humility rests in him, and not only that, but Chesed rests in him. And whoever is not found [united as] male and female has neither fear nor humility nor piety - and therefore he is called "Adam," the sum of all; and since he is called "Adam," Chesed rests in him, as it is written (Psalms 89:3), "I have said, the world shall be built with kindness," and so on - to this point, relevant here. It seems to me that his words concerning "Adam" may be understood by what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 34b) concerning the division of the letters of "Adam" - see there - and by this the rest of the discourse is understood.

And when a person holds fast to all the attributes of Chesed mentioned, and to the other attributes mentioned in the discourse, the holy spirit will rest upon him. And it seems to me that this is what they said, of blessed memory (Bava Batra 25b): whoever wishes to become wise should turn southward - meaning, whoever wishes to merit the attribute of wisdom must hold fast to the attribute of Chesed, called "south," for Chesed is the throne for Chochmah, and by holding fast to the attributes of Chesed, he will certainly merit the Chochmah that is above it.

And in Tanna D'Vei Eliyahu, concerning meriting the holy spirit, he said, in these words, in the Yalkut (Judges, section 42, page 9b), on the verse "and Deborah, a woman, a prophetess" (Judges 4:4): what was the nature of Deborah, that she prophesied over Israel and judged them, when Pinchas the son of Elazar was still living? I call heaven and earth to witness for me: whether gentile or Jew, whether man or woman, whether slave or maidservant, according to a person's deeds, the holy spirit rests upon him. And the rest of his words, concerning the matter of "Lapidot," still need to be copied.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:1-12: We have seen fit, in this chapter, to explain that among the levels a person reaches to become a lover and pious one, he must acquire three attributes: the first, trust [bitachon]; the second, faith [emunah]; the third, joy [simchah]. Trust, as it is said (Psalms 32:10), "but he who trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him."

Faith - Abraham our father, peace be upon him, is the head of the believers, as it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the LORD," and this is the word "emunah" first mentioned in the Torah; and so it is written in Deuteronomy (7:9), "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and kindness," and likewise (Deuteronomy 32:4), "a God of faithfulness, and without iniquity."

And further our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Midrash Shir HaShirim (4:20 [sic]), and likewise in Midrash Shemot Rabbah, on the verse "then sang," in these words: another interpretation, "look [tashuri] from the top of Amanah" (Song of Songs 4:8) - this is Abraham, of whom it is written, "and he believed [ve-he'emin] in the LORD." "From the top of Senir" - this is Isaac; "and Hermon" - this is Jacob - to this point, relevant here.

And so they explained in the Tikkunim (page 5a) concerning "and He shall be the faith [emunat] of your times" (Isaiah 33:6): that "Emunah" is Seder Zera'im [an order of the Mishnah, homiletically] in Chesed, and he says, "Emunah" is the supernal Mother, from the side of Chesed, in whom is the Shema, which is Emunah - to this point.
Joy - as explained in Parashat Vayikra (Zohar, page 8a), that the priest is the one who gladdens, and of him it is said (Psalms 100:2), "serve the LORD with joy."

And let us return to explain each and every one of these on its own, and through this the matter of complete love will be explained to you. Trust is a person's rest and tranquility from worry over the thing he fears, when he considers that thing on which he relies and leans as a shield, a buckler, and a fortified wall - and then he is secure and does not fear that former dread, as he says (Deuteronomy 28:52), "the fortified [walls] in which you trust." And the parable for this: the poor man trusts his heart in the rich man to support him with his charity; so too the mighty man in his might, and the wise man in his wisdom.

And because all these things are from Him, blessed be He - I mean, from His supernal attributes toward us, for He and His attributes are all one - therefore King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 31:15), "but I trusted in You, O LORD," "and I trusted in Your kindness" (ibid. 13:6), "in this I trust" (ibid. 27:3), "my heart trusted in Him, and I was helped" (ibid. 28:7), "trust in Him, and He will act" (ibid. 37:5) - and "in Him" here is like "cast your burden upon the LORD" (ibid. 55:23), which they explained in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei, page 79b) as referring to the things that depend on mazal [fortune], which is "al" [upon]. "I trusted in the kindness of God," and so on (ibid. 52:10); "in God I have trusted, I will not fear" (ibid. 56:5); "happy is the man who trusts in You," and so on (ibid. 84:13); "his heart is steadfast, trusting in the LORD" (ibid. 112:7); "in the fear of the LORD is strong confidence," and so on (Proverbs 14:26); "and he who trusts in the LORD, happy is he" (ibid. 16:20); and so "and he who trusts in the LORD shall be made fat" (ibid. 28:25) - behold, from these verses the place of trust will be explained to you, if you are proficient in the appellations of the attributes explained in the Zohar.

And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, chapter 3) wrote that the premises through which trust is completed for a person are these: first, that he believe that the Creator, blessed be He, has more mercy on a person than any other one who has mercy, and all mercy and compassion shown to him by anyone else are all from God's mercy and compassion, as it is said (Psalms 103:8), "the LORD is merciful and gracious," and it says (Deuteronomy 13:18), "and give you mercy, and have compassion upon you, and multiply you."

And the second, that the modes of a person's benefit are not hidden from the Creator, blessed be He, because He devised the root of man, his form, his constitution, and the order of his composition - He is the Wise One who knows his affairs, his benefits, his harms, and what is good for him both in his world and in his end, as it is written (Isaiah 48:17), "I am the LORD your God, who teaches you to profit, who leads you by the way you should go."

And the third, that the Creator, blessed be He, is mighty, not to be overcome, in what He desires, as it is written (Job 9:4), "wise in heart, and mighty in strength," and His word is decreed above every other thing, and none can reverse His judgment, as it is written, "all that He desired, He has done," and so on, and it says (Isaiah 55:11), "so shall My word be that goes forth from My mouth; it shall not return to Me void." And therefore there is none who can prevent Him from fulfilling the request of one who trusts in Him - for if He were weak, trust would not be complete regarding Him.

And the fourth, that He knows the modes of benefit of the one who trusts, and what is good for him is not hidden from Him, whether in secret or in the open, and He watches over the conduct of all people; He does not abandon them nor is He hidden from them, and nothing of theirs is concealed from Him, as it is written (Psalms 121:3-4), "behold, He who keeps Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep," and it says (Isaiah 40:27), "why do you say, O Jacob, and speak, O Israel, my way is hidden from the LORD," and so on, "have you not known? have you not heard? the everlasting God," and so on.

And the fifth, that He is uniquely devoted to the conduct of the one who trusts in Him, from the beginning of his existence, through his growth, his infancy, his youth, and his old age, to the end of his affairs, as it is written (Deuteronomy 32:6), "is not He your father who acquired you? He made you and established you," and it says (Psalms 22:10), "for You took me out of the womb; You made me trust while on my mother's breasts. I was cast upon You from the womb; from my mother's belly You have been my God," and it says (Job 10:10), "have You not poured me out like milk," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:13-25: And the sixth, that the affairs of the one who trusts are given into His hand - no person can harm him or benefit him, or push away harm from him, except through His power, blessed be He - and he is like an imprisoned servant, who is in a pit, in the net of his master. And when a person feels that no created being can benefit or harm him except by permission of the Creator, blessed be He, his heart shall turn from fearing them and shall trust in the Creator, blessed be He, as it is written (Psalms 146:3), "do not trust in princes," and so on, "happy is he whose help is the God of Jacob, whose hope is in the LORD his God." And it says (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man," and so on (ibid. 17:7), "blessed is the man who trusts in the LORD."

And the seventh, that he know that the One in whom he trusts is the ultimate in generosity and kindness, toward whoever is deserving and whoever is not deserving, and His generosity is constant and His kindness continuous - it is never cut off nor ceases - and a person is obligated in service to Him for the abundant kindness and goodness he received from Him, without his having deserved it or any prior kindness having preceded it, as He says (Job 41:3), "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?" And as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 40:6), "many things have You done, O LORD my God, Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us," and so on, and it says (ibid. 145:9), "the LORD is good to all, and His mercies are over all His works," and it says (ibid. 136:25), "who gives food to all flesh, for His kindness endures forever," and it says (ibid. 145:16), "You open Your hand, and satisfy the desire of every living thing."

And reason dictates that when these seven matters are combined in the Creator, blessed be He, a person's trust in Him should be strengthened, and he should give himself over to Him and not suspect His judgment, nor grow angry at His choice - as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 116:3-4), "trouble and sorrow I found, and I called upon the name of the LORD" - to this point is the summary of his words.

And when you examine these seven matters mentioned, you will find that all these actions are unique to the attribute of Chesed, blessed be He, and especially to the matter of constant providence and the kindnesses that never cease, which are unique to the "open eye" of Arich [Anpin], as it is written in the Idra of Naso (pages 129-130), that this eye neither slumbers nor sleeps, and watches constantly. And it says there that it watches over everything, and everything is sustained through it; and it further says, and this eye is the sustaining of everything - and of this it is written (Proverbs 22:9), "he who has a good eye shall be blessed [yevorach]" - do not read "yevorach" but "yevarech" [shall bless] - for this is called "a good eye," and from it everything is blessed.

And the other actions mentioned, such as (Psalms 22:10), "for You took me out of the womb; You made me trust while on my mother's breasts" - these actions are attributed to the lower Chesed, called "Atah" - "Atah" is the priest forever, and likewise "from my mother's belly, Atah [You have been] my God." And there is a providence attributed to the lower Chesed, for "ra'iyah" [sight] belongs to the right, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 122a), and they gave "the face of a lion" as the sign for the right, and "re'iyah" [sight] is [an anagram of] "aryeh" [lion]. However, this lower providence, which is in the lower eye, sometimes ceases, and therefore the Psalmist said (ibid. 44:24), "awake, why do You sleep, O LORD?" But the supernal providence never ceases.

And therefore, wherever trust is found, it is the aspect of Chesed spreading through all the attributes, and therefore we find trust in supernal Chesed, as it says (ibid. 21:8), "for the king trusts in the LORD, and through the kindness of the Most High he shall not be moved." And even the trust mentioned concerning "Elohim," as he says (ibid. 56:5), "in God [Elohim] I have trusted, I will not fear," and so on - the intent is toward the aspect of Chesed within Elohim, which is "El" from "Elohim," as he says (ibid. 52:10), "I trusted in the kindness of God [Elohim]" - or the intent is toward the general Chesed within the attribute of Elohim, in such a way that whoever trusts in the LORD is fitting that kindness surround him, for Chesed is what spreads, as explained.

And among the conditions of the one who trusts is that he consider and know that the Creator sees his heart, whether his trust in Him is complete or not - for a servant serving before a king of flesh and blood can deceive his heart, but from the Creator, blessed be He, the Fashioner of hearts, nothing is hidden that could deceive Him, as it is written (Psalms 94:11), "the LORD knows the thoughts of man, that they are vanity," and it says (Proverbs 24:12), "does not He who weighs the hearts perceive it?" and it says (2 Chronicles 6:30), "for You alone know the hearts of the children of men." And he should not trust in any person apart from the ability of the Name, as it is written (Jeremiah 17:5), "cursed is the man who trusts in man," and so on, "and whose heart departs from the LORD" - for all the causes that reach him, such as sustenance or his other acquisitions and his healing, are all causes caused by Him, blessed be He, to bring that thing to him. And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot already gave a parable for this in his book (Gate of Trust, chapter 3), likening it to a water wheel that draws water from the well through the prepared vessels - for if one of them is lacking, the drawing of water fails.

Further, I found written a fitting parable for this matter: it is like blind men walking one after another, each placing his hand on his fellow's shoulder, but all are drawn after the first, who sees - and if he should slip away from them, they would all stumble and fall. So it is fitting for a person to think that there is no guide besides Him, blessed be He, the unique One exalted above all, and from Him all the causes and intermediaries are set in motion to bring the desired thing to him - healing through such-and-such a remedy through such-and-such a medicine, and similarly for other worldly matters, like a craft that is a cause for his livelihood - he should not trust in that cause, for if that cause is nullified, his livelihood and sustenance will not be lacking because of it, for the Holy One, blessed be He, will provide his sustenance through another means - like a man splitting wood with an axe: even though the axe cuts the wood, the power does not come from the axe but from the man splitting it, as it is written (Isaiah 10:15), "shall the axe boast itself against him who hews with it?"

And among the matters of trust, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (ibid.) that his providence should be strong and his effort great to fulfill what the Creator obligated him in His service, and to perform His commandments, and to be careful of what He warned him against, so that the Creator agree with him in what he trusts Him for - as they said, of blessed memory (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 4): do His will as your own will, so that He do your will as His own will; nullify your will before His will, and so on. And Scripture says (Psalms 37:3), "trust in the LORD, and do good; dwell in the land, and feed on faithfulness," and it says (Lamentations 3:25), "the LORD is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that seeks Him." But whoever trusts in the Creator while rebelling against Him - how foolish he is, and how weak is his understanding and discernment! For you see that whoever is appointed by people over a matter - when he commands him to occupy himself for the sake of his needs, or warns him about his affairs, and he transgresses his command, and it reaches the one who appointed him that he transgressed his command - this becomes a strong cause preventing him from fulfilling what he trusted him for. All the more so one who has transgressed the statutes and commandments of God, which He has promised and testified about, that the hope of the one who trusts in Him shall be disappointed when he rebels against Him, and he is not fit to be called by the name "one who trusts in God" - rather, he is as Scripture says (Job 27:8), "for what is the hope of the flatterer, though he has gained, when God takes away his soul? will God hear his cry," and so on, and it says (Jeremiah 7:9-10), "will you steal, murder," and so on, "and come and stand before Me in this house?" - to this point. And I say that concerning this it is said (Proverbs 14:16), "but the fool rages, and is confident."

And so it is fitting that he not trust in his wealth, as it is said (ibid. 11:28), "he who trusts in his riches shall fall" - for everything is from Him, as it is said (1 Chronicles 29:14), "for everything comes from You, and of Your own have we given You."

And so among the matters of trust, he should not trust in his good deeds, as though through them he would be saved from the mishaps of the world and bad illnesses - for if so, he would be found consuming his merits - but rather he should trust in His kindness, for his deeds do not suffice to repay the debts owed the Creator upon him, as the pious one elaborated in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust, chapter 4), that even if his deeds were doubled many times over, they would not suffice to repay even one of the Creator's kindnesses to him. Rather, he should think that just as He, blessed be He, gives sustenance to all creatures and to roots, to beasts, animals, and birds - as they said, of blessed memory (Shabbat 107b), He sits and sustains from the horns of the wild oxen to the eggs of lice - just as He has mercy on these not because of their deeds but through His great mercies, so shall He have mercy on him.

The particulars of trust are many, and this is but a small gleaning from what the pious one explained in Chovot HaLevavot (Gate of Trust). And in general, one who trusts is fittingly called "chassid," and is a chariot for the attribute of Chesed, like Abraham - for just as the pious one is called a lover, and it is the way of the lover to be cleaved in love of the Creator, as he says (Proverbs 18:24), "and there is a lover who cleaves closer than a brother," as we elaborated in the previous chapters, and he loves none besides the Creator - so the one who trusts does not trust in created beings, nor place the strength of his affairs upon them, but only upon the Creator. It follows that since his trust in Him is a cleaving to Him, he is a lover of Him - and this is what is explained in Chovot HaLevavot, peace be upon him, that one who trusts is fitting to give himself over to His judgment, like Abraham our father when he was cast into the fiery furnace, and likewise the matter of Chananya, Mishael, and Azaryah, and so on - and we copied his words above (chapter 6).

And so you find concerning Abraham our father, peace be upon him, that he was tested with ten trials, and were it not for his trust in the Creator, blessed be He, and his strength in the cords of his love, he would have rebelled; and it is written (Nehemiah 9:8), "and found his heart faithful before You" - "faithful" [ne'eman] means strong and enduring, unshakeable - and this is the explanation of "ne'eman" found throughout the Torah, such as (1 Kings 11:38), "and I will build for you a sure [ne'eman] house," and the opposite of this (Genesis 45:26), "and his heart fainted, for he did not believe them." And so concerning the fulfillment and strength of a statement, it is said (Numbers 5:22), "and the woman shall say, Amen, Amen." And there is no need to elaborate further on this, for it is simple.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:26-37: It follows that the believer and the truster are both one matter - for the truster too has his heart supported and steadfast concerning the desired thing, in the One who will fulfill it for him, as explained above. And I found written that it is impossible to be a truster if one is not a believer, and faith in God, blessed be He, is what brings him to trust - for since he believes in the Creator, blessed be He, he understands that his success, whether in this world or the World to Come, all comes from Him, and there is none other besides Him - then he sets his heart to trust in Him and to love Him with all his heart.

And the thing that brings a person to be a believer is that he not fear any evil thing, but accept everything that comes upon him with joy - and he is like a servant who knows his master to be generous and good of eye, and at the time he imposes hard labor upon his servants, he then does them great good, elevates them and raises them up, and they become his counselors, eating from his table, riding in his second chariot, and appointed over his treasury. And without doubt, this servant, knowing and recognizing this about his master, will abandon everything in the world in order to do his master's will with joy - and even though that labor is very hard for him to perform, in remembering the good that will come to him because of that labor, everything becomes easy for him. But a servant who sees his master as stingy, and his toil greater than his wage, toils only in sorrow. So it is with this matter: for one who truly believes that everything he does and labors for in the service of the Creator is all for his own good, and the Holy One, blessed be He, will give him a great and good reward for everything he endures for His great Name, and for all the service and ministration he performs for the sake of Heaven He will give him pleasantness in the World to Come - along the lines of what we find concerning Nebuchadnezzar, that for four steps he took in honor of the Creator he merited great greatness in this world (Sanhedrin 96a); and also Esau, for honoring his father and mother, merited greatness in this world, he and his seed after him; and so many similar cases. And there is no doubt that when a person believes all this with a whole heart, he will certainly rejoice in all of God's judgments - for who would not rejoice, giving a penny to charity for the sake of Heaven, and being given in exchange for it, in the World to Come, a talent of gold?

And whoever believes in God with a whole heart will believe in the punishment of the sinner, and will not come to sin - and therefore the whole Torah depends on faith. How so? The beginning of the Torah is (Exodus 20:2), "I am the LORD your God," "you shall have no other gods before Me" - and if he does not believe, what use is his Torah to him? And when a person believes from the depths of his heart that the Creator will fulfill everything written in His Torah, to punish the sinner - and He is a witness - and brings good reward to whoever fulfills His Torah, then he keeps the Torah - for if the thief and the robber knew that they would be killed and would not escape, they would restrain themselves from theft and robbery, but they think and trust that they will be saved - and therefore the whole Torah is entirely bound up with faith, as it is written (Habakkuk 2:4), "but the righteous shall live by his faith," and of Abraham it is said (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in the LORD, and He counted it to him as righteousness" - and concerning all the rest that he did, "righteousness" is not written, but only concerning his faith. And concerning this it is said (Numbers 12:7), "he is faithful in all My house."

And I further say, that all the commandments that depend on tradition require faith - and if he does not believe, he destroys the whole Torah; for if he does not believe that this is the Torah of Moses given to us, and likewise in the tradition of the Scribes who so explained the commandments of sukkah and lulav and the like, then he denies the Torah. Similarly with matters we have by tradition, that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, mentioned in Tractate Berachot (54a) - one who sees the stone on which Moses sat, and the fords of the Jordan, or the place of the altar Elijah made on Carmel - for all these matters depend on tradition, and likewise that this is the Temple and this is Jerusalem and the like - all these require faith; and if he believes in these, his soul will be inflamed with love of the Creator when he remembers the miracles He performed for us in those places, but if he does not believe, certainly he has no love for the Creator.

And they said in the Midrash, brought in the Yalkut (Parashat Beshalach, section 240, page 69c), on the verse "and they believed in the LORD, and in Moses His servant," "and they believed in the LORD" - as a reward for the faith they believed, the holy spirit rested upon them and they said song, as it is written (Exodus 15:1), "then Moses and the children of Israel sang." Rabbi Nechemiah says, from where do you say that whoever accepts upon himself even one commandment in faith is worthy of having the holy spirit rest upon him? For so we find our fathers, as a reward for the faith they believed, and so on - you find that our fathers were redeemed from Egypt only in the merit of faith, as it is said (Exodus 4:31), "and the people believed" - and so it says (Psalms 31:24), "the LORD preserves the faithful."

And further he says: this is the gate of the LORD, the righteous shall enter through it (ibid. 118:20) - concerning the masters of faith, what does it say (Isaiah 26:2)? "Open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith may enter" - through this gate all the masters of faith enter. And so it says (Psalms 92:2), "it is good to give thanks to the LORD" - what brought them to this joy, if not the reward of the faith their fathers believed in this world, which is entirely night? Therefore it is said (ibid. 92:3), "to declare Your kindness in the morning," and so on. And so Jehoshaphat says to the people (2 Chronicles 20:20), "believe in the LORD your God, so shall you be established; believe His prophets, so shall you prosper." "O LORD, are Your eyes not upon faithfulness?" (Jeremiah 5:3); "but the righteous shall live by his faith" (Habakkuk 2:4); "they are new every morning, great is Your faithfulness" (Lamentations 3:23). And so you find that the exiles are gathered in only as a reward for faith, as it is said (Song of Songs 4:8), "with me from Lebanon, my bride," and so on, "look from the top of Amanah," "and I will betroth you to Me forever; and I will betroth you to Me in faithfulness" (Hosea 2:21-22) - behold, how great is faith before Him who spoke and the world came into being, that as a reward for the faith they believed, the holy spirit rested upon them and they said song, as it is said (Exodus 14:31), "and they believed in the LORD, and in Moses His servant... then sang Moses," and so it says (Psalms 106:12), "then they believed His words; they sang His praise" - to this point.

And the reason faith is attributed to Chesed - we have already copied at the beginning of the chapter the words of the Tikkunim (page 5a), that they said that in it is the Shema, which is faith. And the intent is that of the four passages in the tefillin, the third passage is Chesed, and in the third passage we mention the faith of unity, "the LORD our God, the LORD is One" - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained (Parashat Bo, page 43b), whose words we copied above in chapter 5, where he said: the third passage, "Shema," is the secret of the right, called supernal Chesed, which unifies the unity of all in four directions, and the Holy One, blessed be He, arranges through it the order of the whole world, and this is what spreads even into the lower depths - to this point. And through the Chesed that spreads into all created beings, as he said that it spreads even into the depths, created beings believe in Him and in His unity - therefore the word "emunah," first mentioned in the Torah, is mentioned concerning Abraham, as it is said, "and he believed in the LORD" - through Abraham, true faith was revealed in the world, as explained in the Zohar, that Abraham our father, peace be upon him, would make known to all who came into the world that there is a Creator who created everything and whose kindness is present to all.

And through this may be understood what they said in the Zohar (end of Parashat Vayelech), that one who answers "Amen" to every single blessing - just as he thereby opens the supernal gates, the gates of the supernal flow, so they will open for his soul when it departs this world, as it is said (Isaiah 26:2), "open the gates, that the righteous nation which keeps faith [shomer emunim] may enter" - do not read "emunim" but "amenim." And the reason is that the opening of the gates is from the side of Chesed, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 38b), "open for me on the first day," and so too the opening indicated by the vowel points is Chochmah, as explained in the Tikkunim (page 128) - and reason dictates that the King opens gates only from the side of His great kindness and simple will, for from the side of judgment the flow would be closed, and through Chesed it is opened - and this is "You open Your hand" - and since one who answers Amen opens the gates through Chesed, it is fitting that gates be opened for him in the future.

It follows that through His flowing of kindness to us, we fix our faith in Him - and this is what Scripture says (Lamentations 3:23), "they are new every morning, great is Your faithfulness" - for through the kindness He performs with us every morning, in that we deposit with Him the weary soul, and He returns it to us new, and all that weariness it had is gone, and it is a new soul as at the beginning of its creation - behold, this is a great kindness, and this renewal is certainly from the side of Chesed, for the meaning of "who renews in His goodness, every single day, continually, the work of creation" (the Yotzer Or blessing) - and especially in the mornings, which is the "morning of Abraham" (Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim, page 119b). Through this, "great is Your faithfulness" - we have great faith afterward to deposit our souls in His hand every night, in remembering the kindness He does with us.

And let us return to the exposition we were engaged in, that trust and faith are partners with one another - for whoever believes in God with a whole heart will trust in Him with a strong trust, and trust will bring him not to fear anything, and not to serve any person besides the Creator, for He is God, and not to hope in any man, nor agree with them in anything contrary to the service of God, and their affairs will not frighten him, nor will he fear their disputes; and if he rebukes them, he will not be careful of their honor, nor be ashamed of them, nor beautify falsehood for them - as the prophet said (Isaiah 50:7), "for the Lord GOD will help me; therefore I am not confounded." And his trust will bring him to turn away from the affairs of the world and to unify his heart to the matters of Torah and service - and this is possible only if his trust is great in YHVH, and therefore his reward is great, that he be bound in Chesed, as it is written (Psalms 32:10), "but he who trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him." And it says "shall surround him" - meaning, Chesed shall encircle him and clothe him, along the lines of (Exodus 21:8), "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people, seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her" - which is explained in the Sabba (page 96b) as fine garments from the side of the name "Eloah," which is Chesed. And the reason he says "in YHVH" is that YHVH is the root of all the [divine] names and all the modes of existence, and since he places his trust in the essence of all, who sustains all and brings into being it, its spirit, and its soul, he is removed from all the mishaps of the world, and Chesed conceals him from all the masters of judgment, as he says (Psalms 91:2-4), "I will say of the LORD, He is my refuge and my fortress... for He shall deliver you from the snare of the fowler," and so on, "He shall cover you with His pinions, and under His wings shall you take refuge," and so on.

And among the conditions of the faithful and the truster is to be faithful in his service to the Creator, like a peg fixed in a faithful place that will not slip - for the Holy One, blessed be He, is called "the faithful God, who keeps the covenant and kindness," and so on (Deuteronomy 7:9), and His kindness is forever spread to all creatures, and it cannot be conceived that His kindness would slip from His creatures, Heaven forfend, and cease in a moment - rather, the Holy One, blessed be He, made a covenant and a statute in His kindness with His creatures, that His kindness never depart from them - and this is why we find in the Torah "covenant" adjacent to "kindness," along the lines of (Deuteronomy 7:12), "the LORD your God shall keep with you the covenant and the kindness," and so the prophet said (Isaiah 54:10), "for the mountains shall depart," and so on, "but My kindness shall not depart from you, nor shall My covenant of peace be removed," and so on. It follows that whoever is faithful in his words, his commandments, and his Torah is bound to Chesed and to Tzedek [righteousness] as one.

And the Righteous One [Tzaddik/Yesod] is called "faithful" [ne'eman] - for he explained in the Tikkunim (page 34b) and the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Pinchas, page 229a) that in the Righteous One is the secret of "AMeN," which equals 91 in numerical value, like YaHDoNHY [the combined spelling of YHVH and Adonai], and in the Righteous One is this Name, for he is called "all" [kol], in heaven and earth, holding fast in heaven and earth, as they explained in the Tikkunim (page 29a); and in "Amen" he explained, at the end of Parashat Vayelech (page 285b), that it is an acronym for "El Melech Ne'eman" [God, faithful King] - behold, "faithful" is in the Righteous One. It follows that wherever "Amen" is found, as explained in Parashat Vayelech - see there - "faithful" is found. And further, they explained in Tractate Shabbat (page 104a) concerning the [final] nun: "a bent nun, a straight nun" [alluding to a faithful (ne'eman) bent, a faithful (ne'eman) upright].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 12:38-48: It follows, in general, that in all four letters of the Name "faithful" is found, and this is the essence of faith - and therefore the word "emunah," first found in the Torah, is found with the Name YHVH, as he says (Genesis 15:6), "and he believed in YHVH," and so too afterward again (Exodus 14:31), "and they believed in YHVH." And you already know what Rashbi, peace be upon him, said (Tikkunei Zohar, page 92b), that in this Name is the essence of Israel's faith - and we copied his words in the Gate of Fear, chapter 1 - where he said: and therefore the faith of Israel is set in these four letters, in all their appellations they set names for this Name. And he explained there that the Cause of causes unifies the four letters YHVH - it follows that the faithful one is bound to His great Name and to the Cause of causes - happy is he.

And behold, concerning the matter of joy, we have already explained that from trust and faith joy comes - for the servant who trusts in his master and believes he will repay him the reward of his service manifold, will serve with joy, and he is joyful in whatever is decreed upon him, and so he endures everything, like a sick man who eats bitter medicines for the sake of healing - and the one who endures is free from the worries of the world.

Further, there is benefit in joy, as in the story (Ta'anit 22a) of the two men of whom Elijah said that they were destined for the World to Come, because they were men who brought joy - when they saw a sad man, they would cheer him, and when they saw two people quarreling with one another, they would speak jesting words to them until they made peace between them. And so too concerning halachah, one first speaks words of jest, to open the heart to study with joy (Shabbat 30b) - but not the joy of scoffers or the joy of the stingy, but rather a matter of a commandment that gladdens the heart, as it is written (Psalms 19:9), "the precepts of the LORD are right, rejoicing the heart" - and all this is the joy of a commandment.

Upon the attribute of joy depends the positive commandment that one justify His judgment concerning all that befalls him, as it is said (Deuteronomy 8:5), "and you shall know in your heart, that as a man chastens his son, so the LORD your God chastens you." And if, after a person has repented, his affairs do not improve as before, then it is a positive commandment that he consider in his heart that his affairs turned to evil for his own good - for before he repented, the Holy One, blessed be He, was paying the reward of a commandment in order to expel him from the World to Come. And all this depends on the attribute of joy - one who is joyful in his portion, which God, blessed be He, apportioned to him.

But the way for a person to rejoice in his portion is that he rejoice over the evil just as over the good, and endure it with joy - for the one who endures is free from the worries of the world, for the one who endures makes do with the little he has, saying, it is enough for me what the Creator, blessed be He, decrees for me.

And now look and see that joy encompasses everything - for whoever worries over this world has no rest all his days, for he is always thinking of earning money, and does not content himself with what God, blessed be He, has apportioned to him; and therefore whoever rejoices in his portion is rich, even if he is poor, for he rejoices in the Name, for He is his inheritance - as it is written (Lamentations 3:24), "the LORD is my portion, says my soul," and it is written (Psalms 16:5), "the LORD is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup," and so on, and it is said (ibid. 105:3), "let the heart of those who seek the LORD rejoice." And this attribute is only in the souls of the righteous, who are in complete pleasantness in the matter of their service and in great joy in separation, as it is said (ibid. 32:11), "be glad in the LORD and rejoice, O righteous, and shout for joy, all you upright in heart," and it is said (ibid. 97:11), "light is sown for the righteous, and joy for the upright in heart."

Therefore let every person place his joy upon the Torah, and at the time he performs the commandments let him rejoice in his heart that he has merited to be a servant of the supernal King, before whom the sons of the heights bow - and so David said (ibid. 119:162), "I rejoice at Your word, as one who finds great spoil" - and whoever performs a commandment with joy has a thousand times the reward of one who is merely commanded.

Abraham and David were occupied with Torah all day, glorifying and praising with songs and praises of the Holy One, blessed be He, raising their voice in joy - and then all their limbs were saved in their pleasant goodness, and the holy spirit was sent within them, and their heart rejoiced and was filled with love of the Holy One, blessed be He, and their soul was bound in gladness, and secrets and novel insights of the higher realm were revealed to them - because they feared the Name, and pleasantness entered their upright heart. And this is what King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Song of Songs 5:6), "my soul departed at his word," and (Proverbs 23:16), "and my kidneys shall exult when your lips speak upright things." And so David said (Psalms 104:1), "bless the LORD, O my soul" - because the soul ascends upward, and just as it knows the matter of its secret, so it will love the Creator and treasure His commandments; and when the soul reaches its excellent place, to which it is similar, it will then unify Him in His hidden depths and delight in His chambers, and at every time and moment desire His love, and remember Him at night upon its couch - then the Name, blessed be He, sends into it the desire of joy, along the lines of what is said (Isaiah 61:10), "I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my soul shall be joyful in my God" - and happy is the soul that merits to see that joy. And the Shechinah rests only from within joy, and all the prophets did not prophesy whenever they wished, but rather directed their minds and sat joyful and of good heart and secluded themselves - for prophecy rests neither from within sadness nor from within laziness, but from within joy; therefore the sons of the prophets had before them a tambourine, a flute, and a lyre, and sought prophecy - as it is written (2 Kings 3:15), "and it came to pass, when the minstrel played, that the hand of the LORD came upon him."

And love is the glory of the soul, that it glorify itself with the glory of the joy with which it rejoices in its God, and cleave to the radiance of the fear of the Name to cling to the splendor of His majesty; and the light of its yearning for its Creator mingles with the love of its longing, the desire of supernal craving, to crown itself with the crown of beauty of pure, clean thoughts - and it moans from the greatness of the gladness of its rejoicing over its beloved, the supernal Beloved, and it binds itself with bonds of affection, and it seeks and inquires after the levels to shine in the light of life. And at the time it is elevated and made great in the knowledge of the holiness of its Creator, and cleaves in its faith to its Maker, then it spreads out in gladness and rejoicing and expands in joy - at that hour it is sanctified with the holiness of the Holy of Holies, and then it becomes beloved and finds favor before the King of kings of kings, and at that time it is established and beautified and adorned with the splendor, pride, might, and glory of love's beauty - and then the Supernal One treasures it, to make its splendor shine, to bring it into the chambers of radiance, and to bind it in the bond of life. May the Merciful One make us among the people of His service who rejoice in Him.

This chapter I have compiled from Chovot HaLevavot, in the Gate of Trust, and from the book Beit Middot found among us in manuscript, and what I have added to it, according to what the Name has graciously granted me - as the reader will see what is the addition. And it is upon us to entreat the countenance of God, that He guide us on the path of His commandments and His Torah, to be among the lovers of His Name, Amen, and so may it be His will.
With this the chapter and the Gate are concluded:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:1: Before we enter into the explanation of the attributes of repentance, we must explain how many awakenings there are for it - and when a person reads these words from the discourses of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, his heart will be aroused to repent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Repentance 1:2-: Because the Holy One, blessed be He, is abundant in kindness, and created the world in His kindness, freely, without any necessity, because His attribute is to do good, and He desired to do good to existing things and that they recognize His greatness - for this is the essential purpose of the creation of the world, "in order that they know Him," as explained in the Ra'aya Meheimna (Parashat Bo El Paroh, page 42b) - and the creation of the whole world was created only for the sake of Israel, who are called "the first" [reishit] - and this is "in the beginning [bereishit] God created" - for the sake of Israel, who are called "reishit," as it is said (Jeremiah 2:3), "Israel is holy to the LORD, the first-fruits [reishit] of His increase."

And the Holy One, blessed be He, in His wisdom, saw the need for the creation of souls through the good inclination and the evil inclination, so that they receive good reward according to their deeds and according to judgment - for if He created without the evil inclination, it would be an angel, and for this the angels were already created. And there is another reason as well, explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 23a), that since man was created with the evil inclination, it is impossible that he not sin - for few are those, according to the view of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, who died only because of the serpent's poison, in whom no sin was found (Shabbat 55b) - and for this, repentance preceded the creation of the world, as explained in Pirkei D'Rabbi Eliezer (chapter 3), that seven things preceded the world, one of them being repentance.

And so they also said in the Zohar (Parashat Acharei Mot, page 69): we have learned, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world and wished to create man, He took counsel with the Torah.
