It said before Him: You seek to create this man? He is destined to sin before You, he is destined to anger You; if You do to him according to his deeds, this world cannot stand before You, all the more so that man. He said to them, is it for nothing that I am called "merciful and gracious, slow to anger"? And before the Holy One, blessed be He, created the world, He created repentance. He said to Repentance: I wish to create man in the world, on condition that when they repent to you of their sins, you be ready to forgive their sins and to atone for them; and at every single moment, repentance is ready for people, and when people repent of their sins, this repentance returns to the Holy One, blessed be He, and atones for all, and judgments are subdued and all are sweetened, and the person is purified of his sin. When is a person purified of his sin? At the hour he enters into this repentance properly - to this point.

And behold, the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded us concerning the matter of repentance in His holy Torah, through Moses our teacher, peace be upon him (Numbers 5:6), "when a man or woman shall commit any of the sins of man... then they shall confess their sin which they have done, and he shall recompense his guilt with its principal." And it says (Deuteronomy 4:30), "when you are in distress, and all these things have come upon you, in the latter days, if you turn to the LORD your God, and are obedient to His voice - for the LORD your God is a merciful God; He will not fail you, neither destroy you." And in Parashat Atem Nitzavim it says (ibid. 30:1-2), "and it shall come to pass, when all these things have come upon you, the blessing and the curse," and so on, "and you shall call them to mind," and so on, "and shall return to the LORD your God, and shall obey His voice" - and afterward it says (ibid. 30:8), "and you shall return and obey the voice of the LORD" - and it repeats and says, "when you shall return to the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul."

And Ramban, peace be upon him, wrote in his commentary on the Torah (Parashat Nitzavim, page 121), that also the verse "for this commandment" (ibid. 30:11), if it speaks of the Torah, it should have said "all the commandment which I command you this day," and so on. And although this is not really a difficulty, since he explained all these verses as referring to the Torah, which is called "this Torah" (Numbers 19:14) - nevertheless, the Torah has seventy faces, and it is also possible to settle it concerning repentance, since the attribute of "Zot" [This] is also called repentance.

And in my opinion, the verse "for the matter is very near to you, in your mouth and in your heart, to do it" is settled thus: "in your mouth" - the confession of words that must be confessed; "and in your heart" - the acceptance of repentance in his heart and the abandonment of the sin; "to do it" - if it was theft, that he return the stolen item, and the like.

Further, our holy Torah awakened for us an awakening of repentance in Parashat Mishpatim, in these verses (Exodus 21:7-8), "and if a man sells his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out," and so on, "if she is displeasing in the eyes of her master." And it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Mishpatim, end of page 96b), in these words: the Torah, which gives counsel to the whole world, saw this, and warned the people of the world, saying, see how much the Holy One, blessed be He, has compassion upon you - a good pearl that He had, He sold to you for nothing, that you be enslaved to it in this world. "And if a man sells his daughter" - this is the Holy One, blessed be He; "his daughter" - this is the holy soul; "to be a maidservant" - to be a maidservant, enslaved among you in this world - I beg of you, at the time it comes to depart the world, "she shall not go out" like the going out of slaves, that she not go out soiled, that she not go out defiled with sins; let her go out free, pure and clean, so that her Master rejoice in her and be praised through her, and give her good reward in the dewy freshness of the Garden of Eden, as it says (Isaiah 58:11), "and satisfy your soul with dewy freshness" - certainly, when she goes out clean and pure as is fitting. But "if she is displeasing in the eyes of her master" - soiled with the filth of sins, and did not appear before him properly - woe to that body that has lost that soul forever! For when souls ascend pure and go out clean from this world, each and every soul enters into the King's ledger book, all by their names, and it is said, this is the soul of so-and-so, destined to be for that body that it left - and then it is written, "which he has betrothed to him" [asher lo ye'adah], with a vav [meaning "for him"]. But when it goes out displeasing in the eyes of its master, defiled with sins and with the filth of transgressions, then it is written "lo ye'adah" with an alef [meaning "not"], and that body is lost from it, and it is not made available to it.

Except if her Master desires the repentance of the body - then it is written, "then he shall let her be redeemed" [ve-hefdah], as it is said (Job 33:28), "He will redeem his soul from going into the pit." "And he shall let her be redeemed" - this refers to the person whose intent is to redeem it and return in repentance - and in two senses the Holy One, blessed be He, says "and he shall let her be redeemed": through repentance, after he returns in repentance, He redeems it from the path of Gehinnom.

"He shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people" - who is "a foreign people"? The wretched soul, when it leaves the world, and the person went astray from his path with it - it goes to ascend above, into the holy camps, for the holy camps stand on this path of the Garden of Eden, and the foreign camps stand on that path of Gehinnom. If the soul has merit, how many holy camps are prepared to join with it and bring it into the Garden of Eden; if it has no merit, how many foreign camps are prepared on the path of Gehinnom, and these are the camps of the angels of destruction, ready to take vengeance upon it. The verse comes and admonishes: "he shall have no power to sell her to a foreign people" - these are the angels of destruction. "Seeing he has dealt deceitfully with her" - for the soul, whom the Holy One, blessed be He, guards, makes it guarded so that a foreign people not rule over it, within that covering of protection over it.

"And if he betroths her to his son" - come and see how much a person must be careful not to deviate from his path in this world - for if a person merits in this world and guards his soul as is fitting, this is a person in whom the Holy One, blessed be He, delights, and He praises him every day among His retinue, and says, see the holy son I have in that world, thus and thus he acts, thus and thus his deeds are arranged. And when this soul, meritorious, clean, and pure, departs this world, the Holy One, blessed be He, illumines it with several lights every day, calling over it, this is the soul of so-and-so, My son - and this is what is written, "and if he betroths her to his son" - to this point.

This is an awakening for a person along the path of intellect - that since the soul is the daughter of the King of kings of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, and the Holy One, blessed be He, gave it over to man in this world against her will, as explained there - and behold, a person makes use of the soul for the needs of the body, and its descent to this world was only for the repair of Torah and commandments, as is known. And this is what he said, "a good pearl that He had, He sold to you for nothing, that you be enslaved to it in this world" - at the very least, what the Holy One, blessed be He, asked of us is not to soil His deposit through the filth of transgressions.

And if it becomes soiled, that he redeem it at once from the husks, as it is said, "then he shall let her be redeemed" - and through this a foreign people will not rule over it in Gehinnom. And this is a second awakening for a person - that it is fitting he have compassion on the clean pearl the Creator gave him, that it is not fitting to soil it, requiring it to go to Gehinnom to be refined - this is what they said in Tractate Shabbat (page 152b) on the verse (Ecclesiastes 12:7), "and the spirit shall return to God" - give it back to Him as He gave it to you - and the intent is to exclude the filth of iniquities, but not that he give it back to Him without the adornments of Torah and commandments - for if it returns as it came, what did it gain by coming into the world?

Further, a third awakening: it is fitting that he be aroused to repent when he considers that the Shechinah is exiled because of us, as it is written (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away" - and her release from exile depends on our repentance. Why should not each and every one be aroused to repentance, to lighten from her the yoke of exile, and to illumine what he has blemished in her - as we elaborated in the Gate of Fear, how we blemish her and prolong the exile?
